source_text: Adulterari non potest sponsa Christi, incorrupta est et pudica. unam domum nouit, unius cubiculi sanctitatem casto pudore custodit. haec nos Deo seruat, haec filios regno quos generauit adsignat. quisque ab ecclesia segregatus adulterae iungitur a promissis ecclesiae separatur, nec perueniet ad Christi praemia qui reliquit ecclesiam Christi. alienus est, profanus est, hostis est. habere non potest Deum patrem qui ecclesiam non habet matrem. si potuit euadere quisque extra arcam Noe fuit, et qui extra ecclesiam foris fuerit euadit. monet Dominus et dicit: qui non est mecum aduersus me est, et qui non mecum colligit spargit. qui pacem Christi et concordiam rumpit aduersus Christum facit: qui alibi praeter ecclesiam colligit Christi ecclesiam spargit. dicit Dominus: ego et pater unum sumus. et iterum de Patre et Filio et Spiritu sancto scriptum est: et tres unum sunt. et quisquam credit hanc unitatem de diuina firmitate uenientem, sacramentis caelestibus cohaerentem scindi in ecclesia posse et uoluntatum conlidentium diuortio separari? hanc unitatem qui non tenet, non tenet Dei legem, non tenet Patris et Filii fidem, uitam non tenet et salutem.
thought_title: The Church as the one chaste bride and mother; no salvation outside her
orientation: Cyprian is speaking as bishop and author, continuing his argument that the Church is one and that those who break away from her lose Christ and salvation.
pass_a_gloss: To be adulterated [it] is not possible [for the] bride of Christ, incorrupt she is and chaste. one home she knows, of one bedchamber the sanctity with chaste modesty she guards. this [one] us for God keeps, this [one] [the] sons for [the] kingdom whom she has begotten assigns. whoever from [the] church separated to an adulteress is joined from [the] promises of [the] church is separated, nor will he arrive at [the] rewards of Christ who has left [the] church of Christ. an alien he is, profane he is, an enemy he is. to have he cannot God [as] father who [the] church he does not have [as] mother. if he was able to escape anyone who outside [the] ark of Noah was, also he who outside [the] church outside will be escapes. [He] warns [the] Lord and says: he who not is with me against me is, and he who not with me gathers scatters. he who [the] peace of Christ and concord breaks against Christ acts: he who elsewhere beyond [the] church gathers [the] church of Christ scatters. says [the] Lord: I and [the] Father one we are. and again about [the] Father and [the] Son and [the] Holy Spirit [it] is written: and [the] three one they are. and does anyone believe this unity from divine firmness coming, to heavenly sacraments cohering, to be able to be split in [the] church and by [the] divorce of clashing wills to be separated? this unity [he] who not holds, not holds [the] law of God, not holds [the] faith of [the] Father and [the] Son, life not he holds and salvation.

lemmas.gloss: to be defiled, to commit adultery against

choices.english: The bride of Christ cannot be defiled
choices.why: Keeps the passive force of adulterari and the impossibility expressed by non potest; 'defiled' preserves the marital-fidelity metaphor without importing a modern adultery idiom.
rejected: The bride of Christ cannot commit adultery

choices.term: unius cubiculi sanctitatem casto pudore custodit
choices.english: she guards the holiness of one bedchamber with chaste modesty
choices.why: Renders cubiculum as 'bedchamber' to preserve the concrete image of marital fidelity, and keeps the instrumental ablative casto pudore as 'with chaste modesty'.
rejected: she keeps the sanctity of one chamber with pure shame
she guards one bedroom's holiness in chaste shame

choices.term: quisque ab ecclesia segregatus adulterae iungitur
choices.english: Whoever is separated from the Church is joined to an adulteress
choices.why: Preserves the passive 'is separated' and the present 'is joined', keeping the parallel structure of the Latin.
rejected: Anyone separated from the Church joins himself to an adulteress
Whoever has been cut off from the Church unites with an adulteress

choices.term: habere non potest Deum patrem qui ecclesiam non habet matrem
choices.english: He cannot have God as father who does not have the Church as mother
choices.why: Keeps the double accusative construction 'have God as father' and 'have the Church as mother', preserving the exact logical structure.
rejected: He cannot have God for a father who does not have the Church for a mother
No one can have God as Father who does not have the Church as Mother

choices.english: by the divorce of clashing wills
choices.why: Renders conlidentium as 'clashing' to capture the violent collision of wills, and diuortio as 'divorce' to keep the marital metaphor.
rejected: by the separation of conflicting wills
by the divorce of colliding desires

choices.why: Uses the glossary rendering 'sacred signs' for sacramentis and 'cohering' to preserve the present participle's sense of ongoing connection.

bible_refs.note: qui non est mecum aduersus me est, et qui non mecum colligit spargit
et tres unum sunt (the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit)

pass_b_english: The bride of Christ cannot be defiled; she is incorruptible and chaste. She knows one home, and she guards the holiness of one bedchamber with chaste modesty. She keeps us for God; she assigns to the kingdom the children she has borne. Whoever is separated from the Church is joined to an adulteress and is cut off from the promises of the Church. No one who abandons the Church of Christ will arrive at Christ's rewards. He is an outsider, he is profane, he is an enemy. He cannot have God as father who does not have the Church as mother. If anyone outside the ark of Noah could have escaped, then someone outside the Church can escape. The Lord warns and says, "Whoever is not with me is against me, and whoever does not gather with me scatters" (Matthew 12:30). Whoever breaks the peace and harmony of Christ acts against Christ; whoever gathers elsewhere, outside the Church, scatters the Church of Christ. The Lord says, "I and the Father are one" (John 10:30). And again, about the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit, it is written, "And the three are one" (1 John 5:7-8). Does anyone believe that this unity, which comes from divine steadfastness and coheres with heavenly sacred signs, can be split in the Church and separated by the divorce of clashing wills? Whoever does not hold this unity does not hold God's law, does not hold faith in the Father and the Son, does not hold life and salvation.

last_rejected.why: "sacramentis" means mysteries/sacred signs, but "sacred signs" is tautological with "heavenly"; better "heavenly mysteries" or "divine mysteries" to capture the theological weight.
last_rejected.ruling: 'sacramentis' = sacred signs/mysteries; 'heavenly sacred signs' is valid, not tautological. Preference only.

last_rejected.why: The Latin "et" (and) is adversative/rhetorical here, expecting "no one"; "Does anyone" as a genuine question weakens Cyprian's force. Should be "And can anyone believe...?" or "Does anyone really think...?"
last_rejected.ruling: 'et quisquam credit' rendered as rhetorical 'Does anyone believe' preserves force. Omitting 'and' or adding 'really' is mere preference.
